<DOCSTRING>
Unsigns a signed value and validates the timestamp. This method is used to verify the integrity and timeliness of a signed value. If `return_timestamp` is `True`, the timestamp of the signature will be returned as an aware `datetime` in UTC.

Args:
    signed_value (str | bytes): The signed value to be unsinged. This can be a string or bytes object.
    max_age (int | None): The maximum age in seconds for the signature to be considered valid. If `None`, no age check is performed. If the signature is older than `max_age`, a `SignatureExpired` exception will be raised. This parameter helps ensure that the signature is not too old.
    return_timestamp (bool): If `True`, the timestamp of the signature will be returned as a timezone-aware `datetime` in UTC. If `False`, only the unsinged value is returned.

Returns:
    tuple[bytes, datetime] | bytes: The unsinged value and the timestamp if `return_timestamp` is `True`. Otherwise, just the unsinged value.

Raises:
    BadTimeSignature: If the timestamp is missing or malformed. This exception is raised when the timestamp is not present or is not in the expected format.
    SignatureExpired: If the signature age is older than `max_age`. This exception is raised when the signature is older than the specified maximum age.
    BadSignature: If the signature is invalid. This exception is raised by the base class `Signer.unsign` and can be caught to handle signature validation errors.
</DOCSTRING>
